title: Kolay gelsin!
goal: Say the right wish at the right moment: Kolay gelsin, Geçmiş olsun, Hayırlı olsun, Elinize sağlık.

intro.text: Many Turkish wishes are third-person imperatives: *Kolay gelsin* (may it come easy) to someone at work, *Geçmiş olsun* (may it be past) to someone who is ill, *Hayırlı olsun* for something new. After a meal, thank the cook with *Elinize sağlık*.

vocab.en: Hope the work goes well. (said to someone working)
Get well soon. Sorry to hear that. (after illness or bad luck)
Congratulations, all the best. (for something new)
Thank you, that was delicious. (to the cook)
Good luck. All the best. (before a test or a new task)

exercises.question: You walk into a small shop. The owner is busy unpacking boxes. What do you say?

why.1: *Geçmiş olsun* is for illness or bad luck.
why.2: *Afiyet olsun* is for someone who is eating.
why.3: *Hayırlı olsun* is for something new: a home, a job, a car.

exercises.explain: *Kolay gelsin*, **may it come easy**: said to anyone at work.

exercises.question: Your neighbour had a small car accident yesterday. She isn't hurt. What do you say?

why.1: *Kolay gelsin* is for someone at work.
why.2: *Güle güle kullanın* is for something new someone has bought.

exercises.explain: *Geçmiş olsun*, **may it be past**: for an illness, an accident or bad luck.

exercises.en: Ayşe has the flu. — I hope she gets well soon!
Hope the work's going well, Murat Bey.

exercises.question: Your friend shows you the new phone she has just bought. What do you say?

why.1: *Elinize sağlık* thanks someone for food or something they made.

exercises.explain: *Güle güle kullan* to a friend, *kullanın* to someone you call *siz*: **enjoy it**.

exercises.text: Kardeşim kaza yaptı ama iyi, merak etmeyin. — Geçmiş ol___!
exercises.en: My brother had an accident, but he's fine, don't worry. — Sorry to hear that!

reject.why: The vowel of *ol-* is o, a rounded back vowel: four-way harmony gives *-sun*.

accept: Is your exam tomorrow? Good luck!
Your exam is tomorrow? Good luck!
[Is your exam tomorrow|Your exam is tomorrow]? [Best of luck|All the best|Good luck with it]!

exercises.prompt: The meal was delicious, thank you.

exercises.question: Why does Can say *Elinize sağlık*?

context.en: Here you are, enjoy your meal!
It's turned out really well. Thank you, it's delicious.

context.tr: Afiyet olsun. Biraz daha ister misin?
context.en: Enjoy it. Would you like a little more?

options: to thank Selin for the food
exercises.explain: *Elinize sağlık*, **health to your hands**, thanks the cook. The cook answers *Afiyet olsun*.
